items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: I got to know John Lewis at school because he was on the Board of Trustees.

ctx.x: How about personal collections. Have you saved a lot of scores or recordings?

I saved the scores from the Harold Arlen album, because I’m proud of the writing I did for that. That led to something by the way. I got to know John Lewis at school because he was on the Board of Trustees. And when he organized, was a mentor of the American Jazz Orchestra and he did the concerts at Cooper Union, they did a concert based on Harold Arlen and Claude Thornhill, so who was a better natural? And he hired me to conduct, rehearse and conduct. They had — the orchestra was every big name in the city, you…
me I said that’s not a jazz album. He said, “We want the tunes.” He said, “We’re doing Harold Arlen.”
